title: DC Metro concentric map
source_of_truth_note: Declarative source for DC-Metro.svg. The core bundle nests Yellow inside Green; every radius in it derives from the grid-pinned station axis by the slot pitch and the group pitch (see rings).

grid.definition: R = the Capital Beltway radius. Rings marked basis='grid' are exact fractions of R.

off_grid.core-blue: core - 22 (the Blue slot, one pitch inside the station axis)
off_grid.red-inner: core-blue - 32 (one group pitch inside Blue, and the Red arc the Metro Center capsule starts halfway through)
off_grid.core-orange: core + 22 (the Orange slot, one pitch outside the station axis)
off_grid.yellow: core-orange + 32 (the fourth nested core band, one group pitch outside Orange)
off_grid.nc-arc-orange: outer-green - 11 (the rerouted Orange NE arc, one slot offset inside the midway ring)
off_grid.nc-arc-silver: outer-green + 11 (the rerouted Silver NE arc, one slot offset outside it)

grid.note: the core-ring STATION axis is the grid-pinned member of the nested stack, at R/3 = 240 - the axis is pinned like every corridor, and the ink derives at slot multiples off it: Blue 218 and red-inner 186 inside, Orange 262, Yellow 294 and Green 316 outside. Blue, Silver and Orange are one group at the slot pitch, 22, because the mean-slot rule must keep holding, and Yellow and Green are another; the group pitch, 32, is between Orange and Yellow and between Blue and the Red arc. The pitches off the pinned axis are the primary rule for the stack; fractions of R are anchors, not a requirement per ring.

conventions.angle_direction: increasing angle turns clockwise on screen (SVG y-down); 90=south, 180=west, 270=north
conventions.axis_frame: every straight guide is an `axis` = {origin, angle}. A point on it is origin + s*d + n*nrm, where d = (cos a, sin a) and nrm = (-sin a, cos a). `s` is distance along (positive = the axis direction), `n` is the signed perpendicular slot offset.
conventions.sweep: arc `dir`:'cw' = increasing theta (SVG sweep-flag 1); 'ccw' = decreasing theta (sweep-flag 0). large-arc-flag = 1 when |delta| > 180.
conventions.point_continuity: consecutive segments of a line share an endpoint exactly; corners are hard (no fillet) on metro lines. Fillets (r=14) are used only on the Potomac bank trail.

trunk.note: parallel lines in a shared corridor sit at multiples of 11 either side of the corridor axis; adjacent lines are `slot_pitch` 22 apart. A station dot sits at the mean slot of the lines that serve it. `group_pitch` 32 is the spacing between two GROUPS of lines where they run side by side in the core: the Yellow ring is 32 outside the Orange ring, and the Red inner arc is 32 inside the Blue ring. Blue and Yellow on the south corridor are one band at the slot pitch.
trunk.rationale: 22 is tied to the 20-wide stroke (2 px paper gap), not to R, and 32 is the stroke plus 12 of paper. The stroke was 26 and the one pitch 28; the station markers kept their size when the stroke became thinner, so a dot (24) is wider than its line.

minor_dot.note: the marker of a station that only the Purple Line serves (`marker` minor): the station dot at half its size - r 4.3325 and a 3.335 stroke, so it is 12 across, the width of the light-rail stroke, with a white centre of 5.33 - on an `ear`, a black bar across the line through the dot's centre, radial on the ring, 4.5 wide - a little wider than the stroke of the dot's ring (3.335), by eye. The dot's dark ring has little contrast on the purple (2.4:1), so the ears carry the sign: with its round caps the bar reaches 9 from the centre, 1 past the line's casing (8) on each side, where it is black on paper; 3 of black shows past the line's colour on each side. The ten stations between Silver Spring and College Park, 16 apart, keep 4 of the line between two dots and 11.5 between two ears. A label's gap is from the ear's end.

capsule.derivation: casing width = 2*(interchange outer_r + outer_stroke_width/2) = 44; inner width = 2*(outer_r - outer_stroke_width/2) = 32. The interchange ring's outer edge is 22 from its centre, the slot pitch, so a ring or a bar reaches the centrelines of the lines next to its own; the inner dot kept its size when the ring was made smaller for the 20-wide stroke, and 3.6 of white is between the two; the bar runs between the two constituent platform dots.

station_tick.orientation: perpendicular to the line at the dot (radial on a ring, normal to the axis on a straight); centred on the dot
station_tick.derivation: a tick only ever crosses a THREE-line band (the nine Blue/Orange/Silver stops), so its reach is read off the flanking slots: the round caps carry it (length + stroke_width)/2 = 18 from the dot, which is 12 to the near edge of the flanking line's ink (slot pitch 22 - stroke 20/2) plus 6 into it. It used to run 39.83 at 7.5, half-span 23.665, biting one dot radius (8.665) into each flank; shorter and blunter keeps the notch reading as a break in all three lines without eating a third of the outer two.

geo.sliver_note: trail centreline is offset (trail_stroke_width/2 + trail_sliver) = 9.2 outside the water edge, leaving a 3.2 paper sliver.

place.note: the names of places that are not stations and have a sign of their own on paper: the two airports with no Metro station, BWI and Manassas. It is the type of the station subtitles (`secondary`: 12 px, regular, upright, in the ink of the station names), which already name places - National Mall, Kennedy Center, Chinatown - with the two values that straight geography type needs. Not the bold of `minor`, which says Purple Line station, and not the italic of the park and water names.

minor.note: the names of the stations that only the Purple Line serves; a corridor selects it with `font`. 12 px at the station names' own weight, 700 - the subtitle size, two below the 14 of the Metro names. The dense rank's radial names are 16 apart at the line, which leaves about 4 between them there. `baseline_dy` is half the 12 px cap height (8.7) and replaces `constants.label.baseline_dy` for these labels. `wrap_dy` 12 is the line height of a name in two lines: 3.3 of white between the caps of the two lines, as the park names have; it was 13.

water.note: river names: italic type ON the water in a dark blue of the water's own hue (contrast about 7.1:1 on #8DC3E0), at the station names' size. `baseline_dy` is the same 5 that centres the 14 px cap height (10.2) for station labels, applied along the type's own down direction, so the caps sit centred on the point or ring the label names.

park.note: park names: the water names' form in a dark green of the park hue (contrast about 8.5:1 on #CDE0A0), so they read as geography and not as station names. Smaller than the 14 px water names; `baseline_dy` is half the 12 px cap height (8.7) and `wrap_dy` is one font size.

boundary.note: jurisdiction names: spaced italic capitals at the park names' size in the grey of the Beltway's name, one step darker than the boundary's dots.

beltway.note: the Beltway's name, set in capitals at the station names' size, in a grey darker than the ring (contrast about 4.6:1 on paper). `baseline_dy` is the same 5 that centres the 14 px cap height (10.2) elsewhere.

terminal_letter.note: the letter is paper white on the dark line colours and ink on the three light ones (a flat white letter is illegible on #FFD100 and weak on #ED8B00 / #919D9D). Relative luminance cannot separate these cleanly - orange 0.36, silver 0.32, blue 0.31, green 0.32 - so the light set is listed.

station_marks.note: station features, as in the WMATA map's P and H. A station lists its `marks`, and the generator writes them INTO the station's own label line (`marks_line`, default the first title line) as inline glyphs: after the name, or before it when the label is end-anchored, so they sit at the end of the name away from the station. Because a mark is part of the text run, the renderer spaces it against the name with the font it really has - the generator's width estimate is a Helvetica proxy and renderers differ by 5% and more - and on curved type it follows the label's orbit. `gap` is the glyph's dx; `advance` is the room one mark takes, added to a curved line's carrier arc so the mark is not cut off.

parking.note: parking at the station: a white P on a slate background. The background is a real glyph, Inter's own filled square (U+25A0), set at the P's size, 14 px, the size of the station names: in Inter that square is exactly one cap height on the baseline - 10.2 x 10.2 at 14 px - so it is the P's own cap box, and a 3.5 stroke of the same colour grows it by 1.75 all round and rounds its corners: 13.7 x 13.7. `overlay_dx` draws the P back over the square, centre on centre, from Inter Bold's metrics (square: advance 0.909 em, ink 0.091 - 0.819 em; P: advance 0.645 em, ink 0.063 - 0.609 em). `lead_dx` and `tail_dx` add the part of the square that lies outside the two glyphs' advances, so `gap` is measured from the square's visible edges.

hospital.note: a hospital near the station: a white cross on a red background. The background is the same square as the parking mark's, 13.7 x 13.7 with its stroke. The cross is Inter Bold's plus sign at 14 px, 7.0 x 7.0. The plain plus stands 0.5 - 7.5 above the baseline, 1.1 below the square's centre (5.1), so `features` asks for Inter's capital form (OpenType `case`), which the font lifts to the middle of the cap height - the square's centre. A fallback font without that form shows the cross 1.1 low. `overlay_dx` centres it sideways from the font's metrics (plus: advance 0.673 em, ink 0.086 - 0.587 em).

label_diagonal.note: the two rotations used for dense label runs; -52.25 = 37.75 - 90. 37.75 also matches the Potomac west-bank angle.

label.distance_note: The default label gap, in px of white paper, used wherever a corridor or run does not declare `distance` of its own. `distance` is a GAP, not an offset from the corridor axis: it is the clearance between the leading edge of the block of type and the FURTHEST-PROTRUDING ink at the station, along the label's own offset direction. Two obstructions are measured and the larger wins — (a) the station's own marker's outer edge (dot r + stroke/2 = 12.0, terminal 14, interchange outer ring 22, capsule bar half-width 22; a multi-platform station uses its extreme dot on the label's side) and (b) the outer casing edge of the band of lines the station sits in, which is the outermost slot the station's own lines run in plus half the casing width (20/2 + 2 = 12). The block's own optical half-depth, `baseline_dy + extra/2` projected onto the offset direction, is solved out too, so a wrapped label keeps the same gap a single-line one has (the block-centring lift would otherwise spend half its extra advance on it). One number therefore reads as the same white gap under a plain dot, an interchange ring, a terminal circle and a capsule alike, and on a far slot as on the mean one — which is what a per-corridor offset from the axis could not do: on `W` the Orange-only stops sat 24 px further off their dots than the Orange/Silver ones. See SPEC.md §6.2. In the ring frame the band term is just the casing half-width, the station's own line running through its dot; a CONCENTRIC NEIGHBOUR of that ring is not counted, which is why `CORE` — three rings 22 apart — declares a `distance` of its own.
label.aim_note: A label's gap fixes where its base point sits ACROSS the corridor; where it sits ALONG the corridor is `ds` plus a derived slide, the one that hugs the NEAR END of the label's FIRST LINE to its own station's dot. Which end is near is `text-anchor`'s answer, and the two anchors want different geometry. END-anchored, the block finishes on the base point and runs back up the reading line away from the station, so aiming it is putting that READING LINE through the dot centre — solve (aimed - dot)·down = 0. `W` needs it: type turned -52.25° and hung 36 px below the band reads back up into the corridor 27.9 px further on, so a label that finishes square under its dot aims a half-span past it and the whole rank reads as if it belonged to the next station along. START-anchored, the block BEGINS on the base point, so the same reading-line rule solves for the far intersection: on `E` (type at 37.75° above a horizontal corridor) it stood the anchor 66 px down the line PAST the dot and shoved the whole rank outward, worst at the map edge. A start anchor wants to begin DIRECTLY BELOW its own dot in the corridor frame instead — solve (aimed - dot)·along = 0 — which stands the first letter square under the marker and leaves `distance` alone to say how far off it the words sit. The dot's perpendicular foot on the baseline is not that point either: it is measured across the type rather than across the corridor, and on `E` it left the same rank about 25 px back up the corridor from its stations. Middle-anchored type keeps the reading-line rule. `aimed` is the FIRST line's optical centre, base - (extra/2)·down, not the base point: the base point centres the WHOLE block, which a wrapped label carries half its extra advance further down, and a slanted reading line taken from there lands short of the dot by that drop over the tangent. On `W` that left the three subtitled labels - Vienna, Dunn Loring, West Falls Church - 7 px back down the corridor from their own dots while the five single-line labels of the same rank aimed true. Aiming the first line puts a wrapped label exactly where a single-line one at the same station would sit; the lift is 0 for a single-line label, so nothing else moves. The slide is solved in the same fixed point as the gap and moves the base point along the corridor only, so the white gap of `distance` is untouched by construction. It applies to the two modes whose reading line is straight: `straight` and `radial`. Concentric type is set on a circle about the map centre, and a circle offset from a station never passes through it whatever the slide — the counterpart there is angular (the anchor at the dot's own θ), which a ring station has by construction and a spoke station cannot have at all, so concentric labels are left where the gap puts them. The end rule divides by the sine of the angle between the type and the corridor and the start rule by `along·along` = 1, so only the first has a denominator that can vanish; the straight modes are still held OBLIQUE to the corridor, `aim_degenerate_dot` being the magnitude below which either the sine or the cosine is declared degenerate and no slide is made. Type reading ALONG its corridor (|along·down| below it) is already square beside its marker and sliding it only slides it down its own reading line: L’Enfant Plaza on the east trunk and New Carrollton on its radial exit. Type reading ACROSS it (|along·reading| below it) is set square across the corridor, its `distance` — which acts along the reading direction there — has already answered where the words start, and its radial offset carries them nowhere along the corridor to correct: the seven `outer-green` radial labels, which read across their ring, and Rosslyn and Smithsonian on the core arcs. Eight of the nine radial labels therefore carry no aim; Minnesota Av, the one oblique to its own corridor, does, as do 22 of the 25 straight ones - 23 aimed labels in all, which `--census` counts. See SPEC.md §6.2.
label.curve_note: `curve_default` is the label curve mode used wherever a corridor, run or station does not declare `curve`. The three modes: "concentric" sets each line of type on a circle segment about the map centre through that line's baseline point; "radial" sets it straight along the radius from the centre through that point, turned by the station's own angle normalised into (-90, 90] so the glyphs stay upright, which makes the arm read as a sunburst; "straight" is the flat text + `rotate` behaviour. Under "concentric" the arc's own tangent is the rotation, so `rotate` no longer turns any glyph — it survives only as the nominal reading direction rule A derives `side` from; under "radial" the radius supplies the rotation the same way, `side` still signs `distance`, and `align` is re-derived from the true radial reading direction so the text block always sits outward of the marker (`start` on the right half, `end` on the left, where the upright flip reverses the reading direction). Note that `distance` and `ds` are measured against the CORRIDOR, not against the reading direction, so changing a corridor's or run's `curve` changes which of the two ends up perpendicular to the type and therefore reads as a vertical offset of the words from their dot — re-examine both whenever `curve` changes (SPEC.md §6.7). `curve_pad_px` is the slack added to the estimated advance of each line so that a text run can never outgrow its arc and be truncated; the estimate itself comes from generate.py's ADVANCE_PER_MILLE table (Helvetica-Bold advances as an Inter proxy) times ADVANCE_SAFETY.
label.note: Placement constants shared by every label. `baseline_dy` centres the 14 px/700 cap height on the dot line (cap height 10.2, half 5.1, drawn as 5) and is applied along the label's own down direction, so it rotates with the text — radially inward or outward under `curve` = concentric, where down is the radial, and tangentially under `curve` = radial, where down is the tangent. `block_centring` lifts a multi-line label by half the advance of the lines after the first, keeping the block centred on the dot. `rule_a_degenerate_dot` is the |cos| below which the outward radial is too close to perpendicular to the reading direction for rule A to decide a side; those corridors/runs must declare `side` (generate.py enforces it).

nc-exit.note: Radial exit from the rerouted Orange/Silver arc out to New Carrollton on the Beltway. The angle is DERIVED from the arc, not authored. The arc's inner end is Minnesota Av - the ring crossing of an OFFSET axis, hence the corner where the two lines leave `nc-diagonal` for the ring, and a point that swings as `outer-green` moves: 648 put it at theta=350.6413, 612 put it at 353.0963, and 632 - the radius the Branch Av arm now also has - puts it at 351.6884. From there the arc steps at 4 deg, the step the Branch Av arm takes on this same ring, so the two outer arcs read at one spacing - 44.12 px between stations at r=632. Four steps carry Deanwood, Cheverly and Landover to 347.6884, 343.6884 and 339.6884 and land this exit at 335.6884; move the ring and the whole ladder re-solves off the new corner. The dependency between this exit and the Anacostia river band used to run the other way: the exit was pinned to the band's north-east terminus at theta=330.6441, which forced 5.6138 deg steps, nearly twice Branch Av's. dulles-leg.note: Silver Dulles arm, PARALLEL TO THE POTOMAC and anchored at Spring Hill, which is the arc's far end and this axis's origin, so the run starts at s = 0. 217.7534 is the river's west-bank angle (37.7534) turned outbound; `constants.label_diagonal.angle` carries the same 37.75. tysons-leg.note: Silver Tysons -> East Falls Church leg. Origin, angle (36.7833) and length 186.8716 are all DERIVED from the Tysons corner on the Beltway (theta 185.4111) and the west-trunk Silver slot at s=567.125; McLean carries the leg's one explicit page spacing.

bwi.note: the radius that the MARC and Amtrak line to BWI goes out on. 330 is on the 1.5 deg angle grid and is the one free radius in this quarter from Union Station's ring to the canvas: it passes 17 from NoMa-Gallaudet U's name, 25 from Rhode Island Av's, west of the Anacostia's end (333.4), 43 from Glenridge's name, 24 from New Carrollton's Purple terminal and 12 from the start of New Carrollton's name.

vre-union.note: VRE at Union Station: the radius through the middle of the station's VRE badge (r 417.91), the leg of the L from the badge in to `vre-union-ring` (388.5), about 22.5 long; Judiciary Sq's name is moved in along its spoke to make room.

vre-lenfant.note: VRE to L'Enfant Plaza: level, below the east trunk's casing (the Blue Line's, y 1056), from the `vre-union-ring` ring west to L'Enfant Plaza's VRE badge, under the station's two circles at x 1260.19, across the Green and Yellow lines. The badge is on the middle slot (y 1062); the line is on the `top` slot (y 1059.5), so the line's top edge (y 1057.5) is 2 below the badge's top edge (y 1055.5), and its casing's top is 0.5 below the Blue Line's casing. The ring across the river (`vre-potomac`) leaves it at x 1270.22, under the badge's east end.

vre-cross.note: the radius on which the VRE line to Manassas turns south from its ring under King St-Old Town's name (`vre-king`) and crosses the Beltway to the outer ring (`vre-outer`), half a spacing (6.91 deg) before Rolling Road's tick there. On the ground the line crosses the Beltway between Backlick Road, which is just inside it, and Rolling Road.

vre-alexandria.note: VRE to Alexandria: one vertical straight at x 1011, EAST of the Yellow line, as the railway is east of the Metro through Crystal City: its white edge is 3 from the Yellow line's casing (x 1005) and 3 from the DCA apron and the Old Town area (from x 1017, both moved 12.25 east to make the room), over the bank trail. It runs from the `vre-potomac` ring at the river's bank (s -265.77, theta 87.63, the `neg` branch) down through Crystal City's VRE badge (s -415.31, level with the station) and King St-Old Town's (s -689.66, the end of the station's name below it), to the `vre-king` ring (theta 89.1), on which the Manassas Line turns west across the Yellow and Blue lines south of King St-Old Town. `s` is 1000 - y.

marc-brunswick-in.note: MARC's Brunswick Line from Bethesda to Rockville, very close beside the Red Line, as on the ground, where the railway and the Red Line run side by side towards Rockville: parallel to the Red Line's radius, 28 west of it - the origin is the map's centre moved 28 across (n = -28), so the middle slot is the line and ticks, which are placed on an axis's centre line, sit on it; `s` is measured as on the Red Line's radius, from the Silver Spring ring (`marc-silver-spring`) to Rockville's badge ring (`marc-rockville`). 28 is the least that clears Bethesda's transfer marker (ink to 22): the line's edge is 4 from it, 14 from the Red Line's casing and 14 from the dots of Medical Center to Rockville.

marc-brunswick-out.note: MARC's Brunswick Line: one radius from the Rockville ring (`marc-rockville`, r 892.8) out to Martinsburg. 224.5 deg is 6.5 deg from the Red Line (231), nearer it than the middle between the Red Line and the Potomac's north bank (`geo.water.potomac.nw_arm.north_bank_edge`), which was too near the river: 101.1 from the Red Line at r 892.8 and 178.8 from the bank at r 1076.7, where Martinsburg was before.

vre-south.note: VRE's Fredericksburg Line: vertical, down from the centre of Franconia-Springfield's terminal to the canvas's bottom edge.

hef-out.note: the last leg of the VRE line: horizontal, at the y of the Manassas airport's apron (1238.5), from the apron east to the `vre-outer` ring, which it meets at theta 161.47. All of it is outside the Beltway. Its origin is the apron's centre.

blue-franconia.note: Blue Franconia branch, a RADIAL spoke from the map centre at 106.5 - on the 1.5 deg angle grid and the nearest grid angle to where Van Dorn St already stood (107.225). Built like `nc-exit`: the line runs in from Franconia-Springfield at s = 800 (the Beltway plus 80), crosses the Beltway at Van Dorn St, and meets the `blue-arc` ring at 659.6728, where it turns onto the arc and sweeps 13.9804 deg ccw to the south corridor's Blue slot at theta 92.5196 - King St-Old Town's own latitude, so the turn happens at the station rather than 9.5299 north of it as the old straight join did. It replaces a VERTICAL axis at x=786.7894 whose offset was solved to open the Van Dorn -> Eisenhower Av gap to 1.3x its previous value; that derivation is gone with the axis, and the gap is now whatever the two pins make it. Van Dorn moves 9.11 and Franconia-Springfield 14.05.

red-nw-spoke.note: the seven stations inside Bethesda, the last of them Friendship Heights at 600. Bethesda left this run for the `purple` ring (672), 72 out, and the six stations past it are `red-nw-outer`.

red-nw-outer.note: Medical Center to Shady Grove. Both ends are pinned, so the step is solved from them: s0 = the Beltway (720), so Medical Center is ON the Beltway, as Forest Glen is on `red-north-outer`, and Shady Grove stays at 936, the end of the line - five steps of 43.2. On the Beltway the dot is 14 from Bethesda's marker. It stood at 748 (beltway + 28) before, with a step of 37.6.

red-north-spoke.note: Beltway passes BETWEEN Silver Spring and Forest Glen. The step was 96; 114 puts Silver Spring on the `purple` ring (672), where the Purple Line crosses the spoke. Its transfer marker reaches 699.4, 18 below the Beltway, and Forest Glen is 76 further out.

red-north-outer.note: a run of its own rather than the tail of `red-north-spoke`: that run's step of 114 is what puts Silver Spring on the `purple` ring, and this arm is a little closer outside the Beltway. s0 = the Beltway (720), so Forest Glen is ON the Beltway, as Medical Center is on `red-nw-outer`, 48 past Silver Spring (672); the step of 74 puts Wheaton at 794 and Glenmont at 868 (y = 132), and its terminal's top at y = 117.5 is 57.5 below the canvas's 60 margin; nothing is above it. The Red line's route ends at the literal s = 868 on `north`, so a change here must move that end too. Forest Glen stood at 748 (beltway + 28) with a step of 60 before; a step of 48 made the arm look compressed, and 76, one even ladder from Silver Spring, was also tried.

red-ne-spoke.note: the last station, Brookland-CUA, is held on the major ring (558), and Judiciary Sq, the first, is at 380: 75 past Gallery Place on `yg-seam` (305), by eye - at 61 its name was only about 7 above Gallery Place's two-line name. The four steps from there are 44.5 each. Five equal steps of 50.6 from Gallery Place would put Judiciary Sq's name on Gallery Place's. The run was 390 and four steps of 42, with 85 between Gallery Place and Judiciary Sq.

ne-diagonal-inner.note: the outer end is pinned, so the step is solved from it: Mt Vernon Sq carries the arm's explicit page spacing at s = 350 and Fort Totten sits on the major ring at 558, which divides the remainder into five equal steps of 41.6 - the last of them landing on Fort Totten itself, so the arm reads at one spacing all the way out. `distance` 2 puts the labels 2 from the casing of the two lines, where the default gap is 4: the dot is in the middle of the Yellow and Green lines, 23 from that casing, so a label is far from its dot, as on the south corridor. `ds` -0.75 puts the middle of the type on each station's own circle, within 0.15. rule A is degenerate on this spoke (tangential type), so `side` must be declared; left sends the Mt Vernon Sq to Georgia Av-Petworth stack west, away from the Red spoke, while the outer half of the diagonal reads east.

ne-diagonal-outer.note: `distance` 2 and `ds` -0.6 put the two labels 2 from the lines' casing and the middle of their type on the stations' own circles; at `ds` 1 the type was 1.7 outside them. West Hyattsville and Hyattsville Crossing, between two transfer markers: Fort Totten on the major ring (558) and College Park on the `purple` ring (672), which left this run when the Purple Line made it a transfer station. Both ends are pinned, so the run is solved from them: each end station is 43 from its transfer station - the marker's 27.4 and the dot's 12 with 3.6 of white - and the step is the slot pitch, 28, which leaves 4 between the two dots. The run was 612, 648, 684 at a step of 36; a transfer marker at 684 would have touched Greenbelt's terminal, 36 further out. West Hyattsville's dot now reaches 589, 1 inside the DC boundary (590), as Friendship Heights' does.

west-trunk-outer.note: both ends pinned, so the step is solved from them: s0 is East Falls Church's s on the trunk and the far end is the Beltway cut by the Orange slot, sqrt(720^2 - 22^2) = 719.6638, which halves into two steps of 76.2694. Vienna rides one step past the Beltway at i 3, s = 795.9332, which is what makes the arm read at ONE spacing all the way out; it used to sit at an explicit 762.0, only 42.5446 past Dunn Loring against the run's step. Indices 0 and 2 carry no station of their own - East Falls Church is placed by `west-trunk-inner` i 4 on the mean slot and Dunn Loring by `at_ring` beltway - but both land on the run's own arithmetic, which is what pins the two ends.

east-trunk-outer.note: `ds` 0.0: the along-corridor placement is the derived aim, and the run's wrapped Addison Rd / Seat Pleasant block gets its block-centring lift back out of the gap rather than out of a hand nudge.

south-leg.note: one even ladder the whole way, Pentagon to Huntington, on two pins. s0 = Pentagon = the Yellow ring (294) cut by the south axis CENTRELINE, sqrt(294^2 - 18^2) = 293.4485. The outer pin is EISENHOWER AV ON THE BELTWAY: the axis's Yellow slot cuts r=720 at sqrt(720^2 - 7^2) = 719.966, and Eisenhower is the seventh step, so step = (719.966 - 293.4485)/7, carried at 60.9311. Huntington is not pinned at all now: it rides one more step to 780.8973 and the Yellow line's free end follows it there. It used to sit at 768.27, level with Franconia-Springfield on the map's bottom baseline; that pairing is what this spacing costs.

dulles-leg.note: s0 = the Beltway, i.e. Greensboro is the crossing point and the innermost station on the straight arm; the run steps OUTWARD from there, so Ashburn lands at 720 + 8*37.5 = 1020. Tysons is not on this run - it is a ring station on the Beltway at the far end of the concentric link (see `stations`).

green-se-inner.note: the leg join, and the inner half of a spoke that is deliberately UNEVEN: close at both ends and open across the river. s0 sets Waterfront 72.8657 out from the Green ring (324) and the step carries Navy Yard-Ballpark 56.8657 further, to 453.7314, where the arm stops short of the Anacostia park band (508 - 572). That dot's ink ends at 465.73, 42.3 clear of the band's inner edge, and the 124.8657 on to Anacostia is the river crossing - the gap is the point, not a spacing failure. The earlier ladder solved three equal steps of 82.8657 from the ring to Anacostia and left only 6.3 of white between Navy Yard-Ballpark and the band, which is what this replaces. `curve` concentric sets Waterfront's and Navy Yard-Ballpark's type off the spoke rather than out along it; rule A derives `right` for them, the flank opposite `green-se-outer`'s declared left. `ds` 0.0 is what concentric wants - a slide there acts ACROSS the type and would lift the words off their own dots.

green-se-outer.note: the outer half, past the river, and a run rather than two loose {axis, s} stations so that Anacostia and Congress Heights have somewhere to declare their label side and curve. s0 = 584 puts Anacostia just clear of the park band's outer edge of 572: the dot's ink reaches back to 572.0. At the earlier 578.5971 it crossed the band by 5.4. The 46.7455 step is solved BACKWARDS from Congress Heights, which holds 1.2545 inside the arm's ring: when `outer-green` and the Congress Heights - Branch Av arm on it were moved out by 20, from 612 to 632, Congress Heights went with it to 630.7455 and Anacostia did not. `curve` concentric because radial type cannot separate two stations that share an angle - theirs lay 0.1 deg apart on one another. `side` left is declared against rule A, which would put both on top of Southern Av, and it is the flank opposite `green-se-inner`'s derived right, which is what keeps the spoke's four labels clear of each other. `ds` 0.0 is what concentric wants.

CORE.name: Core ring (Blue/Orange/Silver)
CORE.note: `side` left is declared because rule A would send Federal Triangle straight into Archives; reading inward over the Mall is what the ring wants. The `distance` of 9.0 is the one corridor gap of its own: a concentric NEIGHBOUR ring is not part of a station's band, and these seven stations sit in a stack of three rings 22 apart.

W.name: West trunk (Vienna – Rosslyn)
W.note: `curve` straight: at theta ~172-178 deg a concentric arc stands almost vertical, so eight labels would rise through the band they belong to; the -52.25 slant hangs them in one diagonal rank clear below it. Rule A derives `left`, hence end-anchored type reading up-right into its own station. `ds` 0.0 because the along-corridor slide is now the derived aim, and a rank is aimed, not nudged.

E.name: East trunk (L’Enfant Plaza – Downtown Largo)
E.note: `curve` straight for the same reason as `W`: at theta ~0-6 deg the core arcs stand near-vertical and eleven labels would rise through their own band; the 37.75 slant ranks them below it. Rule A derives `right`, hence start-anchored type reading down-right out of its station. `ds` 0.0 — the slide is the derived aim.

S.name: South corridor (Pentagon – Huntington)
S.note: `side` left is declared because rule A is near-degenerate (axis 18 px west of centre).

NE.name: Yellow/Green north-east diagonal (Greenbelt)
NE.note: rule A is degenerate here (tangential type on a radial spoke) so `side` must be declared; right sends the outer stack east.

RNE.name: Red north-east spoke
RNE.note: rule A is degenerate (tangential type on a radial spoke) so `side` is declared; right reads east off the spoke.

RN.name: Red north spoke (Glenmont)
RN.note: rule A is degenerate — a due-north spoke under unrotated text — so `side` is declared; left reads the Glenmont arm west off its own spoke, away from the Purple Line's dense rank east of Silver Spring.

MJR.name: Major ring – red arc (Takoma)
MJR.note: rule A is degenerate — due north under unrotated text — so `side` is declared; right keeps this label on the same flank as the rest of the Red north arm.

RNW.name: Red north-west spoke (Shady Grove)
RNW.note: not degenerate — rule A resolves `left` here. `side` right is declared against it so the fourteen Shady Grove labels read inboard, off the far side of their own spoke, the way the Glenmont arm does.

SNW.name: Silver north-west spoke (Ashburn)
SNW.note: `side` right is declared against rule A, which would throw the Dulles arm's labels back across their own dots and down the leg. `curve` straight for the same reason `MJS` takes it: without it the arm's labels default to concentric and ignore this `rotate`.

MJS.name: Silver Tysons run
MJS.note: `side` right is declared against rule A, which would throw these labels back across their own dots and down the leg, as it would on `SNW`. `curve` straight is declared here rather than per station: with no curve these labels fall to the default concentric, which derives its own turn off an arc and ignores `rotate`, so they read at a different angle from Vienna and Dunn Loring, whose `W` sets straight. `ds` 0 for the same reason it is 0 on `W`: type set ACROSS its corridor is aim-degenerate (|along.reading| = 0.033 here, under the 0.1 threshold), so no derived slide opposes `ds` and any value in it is a raw shift along the leg.

GSE.name: Green south-east spoke (Branch Av)
GSE.note: `curve` radial: the `outer-green` ring stations of the Branch Av arm sit 4 deg apart at one radius, where concentric type piles up; a sunburst separates them by angle. Branch Av takes it too, at the far END of `green-se-exit` with open paper past the Beltway, as New Carrollton does. Naylor Rd and Suitland override it, because there radial type reads along the exit. `ds` 0.0 is what that mode wants — under `radial` a slide acts ACROSS the type on a ring station, so the clearance is `distance`'s job alone.

MJOS.name: Orange/Silver New Carrollton branch: diagonal out to Minnesota Av, concentric arc to Landover, radial exit to New Carrollton
MJOS.note: `curve` radial: Deanwood, Cheverly and Landover are ring stations 4 deg apart at one radius, where concentric type piles up into a single run-on string; a sunburst separates them by angle, as it does for GSE's four `outer-green` stations, whose 4 deg step these now share. The two frames disagree about this arm's band, so the two AXIS-placed stations carry a `distance` of their own against the corridor's 13. Minnesota Av and New Carrollton read the whole band off their axis slots - 11 out to the Silver slot plus 12 of casing, an `extent` of 23 - while the three RING stations read only their own dot, an `extent` of 12, the ring frame counting no concentric neighbour (see `band_offsets`). That rule is right for GSE, where Green really does run on `outer-green`, and wrong here: this arm's lines run on `nc-arc-orange` (621) and `nc-arc-silver` (643) while the dots sit on 632, a ring with no ink on it. So the corridor's `distance` carries the missing 11 for the three: 13 puts their names 25 off their dots, at r = 657, 2 outside the Silver line's casing (655), and Minnesota Av's own 2 puts it at the same 25 - the 2 that the labels of the other two-line stretches keep from their casing. The two corridor-frame stations (Minnesota Av, New Carrollton) take the same mode, `curve` being independent of frame - it re-derives `rotate` from each base point's own theta whether that point comes off an axis or off a ring. `ds` 0.0 is what that mode wants: under `radial` a slide acts ACROSS the type on a ring station, so the clearance is `distance`'s job alone, and one number would otherwise mean two different things inside one corridor.

MJB.name: Blue Franconia branch
MJB.note: the branch is a RADIAL spoke now, so its type is set ACROSS the spoke, not along it - the default `concentric`, as `RNW` and the other radial spokes take. `curve` radial was tried and is wrong here for the reason it is right on `MJOS`: radial type reads out along the outward radial, which on a spoke IS the line, so Van Dorn St read down its own track and through Franconia-Springfield's terminal. New Carrollton can carry it because it sits at the far END of its spoke, with open paper beyond.

PW.name: Purple Line west arc (Connecticut Av – 16th St-Woodside)
PW.note: three stations 9.75 deg (114 px) apart on the `purple` ring, with room for a name along the line: concentric type centred on its own station (`align` middle), in the `minor` font. `side` left is the outer side here - west of north the outward radial points against the nominal reading direction - so the names stand 4 above the casing, in the white between the line and the Beltway.

PN.name: Purple Line dense rank (Silver Spring Library – Baltimore Av-UMD)
PN.note: ten stations 1.375 deg (16 px) apart on the `purple` ring, between the transfer markers of Silver Spring and College Park: the first and the last are 36 from their transfer station (the marker's 27.4, the dot's 5 and 3.4 of white). Type along the line has no room, so the names are a sunburst (`curve` radial) on the OUTER side, as on the rest of the line: `side` right is outward east of north, and the radial mode's own anchor runs the words out from the station. `ds` -2 slides every name 2 west along the line, across its own type, an optical correction to where the names stand on their dots. The Beltway is 32 above the casing, so every name crosses it, and `halo` 4 puts 2 of paper white round the letters, which breaks the ring under each name - as the thirteen other stations whose names cross the Beltway have in a `halo` of their own, and Greensboro and Spring Hill. Every name is one line. The longest, Adelphi Rd-UMGC-UMD (101 long), ends at r = 786; Silver Spring Library (86) passes 21 east of Forest Glen's dot.

PE.name: Purple Line east arc (Riverdale Park North-UMD – Glenridge)
PE.note: four stations 8.721 deg (102 px) apart on the `purple` ring, the five equal parts of the arc from College Park (288.5) to the exit's corner (332.1051). Names as on `PW`, on the outer side, which is `side` right east of north: they stand 4 above the casing (681), in the 36 of white below the Beltway, and all that have two words are two lines.

lines.name: Silver · New Carrollton spur
lines.note: the inner stub is coincident with the main Silver line - same axis, same slot - so it is never seen; s0 only has to sit outboard of that line's riser onto the slot (s = 240) and inboard of the `nc-diagonal` branch point, and 330 is inside Federal Center SW at 349.91.

lines.name: MARC Penn Line and Amtrak to BWI
lines.note: a trial: the MARC Penn Line, which Amtrak also uses, from Union Station to BWI Marshall Airport. It is not a Metro line, so it is a thin solid line - 4 wide - in the red of the MARC badge (#B7414E), with a white casing 1 wider on each side (`casing_width` 6), as all the commuter lines have, so that where it is drawn over another line or the geography a thin white edge shows which is on top, and its stations are ticks. The commuter lines were dashed while they were only starts; now that they have all their stations, they are solid. The red is the Penn Line's own colour on MARC's system map of 2020, where the Camden Line is orange and the Brunswick Line yellow, and it is the red of that map's heading. It is written from the airport in: clockwise on the ring `marc-bwi-ring` (r 830) from BWI's stopper at theta 314 to the `bwi` radius (an arc may open a path with a `from` angle), then in along that radius past New Carrollton (r 759.1) to the `marc-union` ring, and counter-clockwise on that ring to theta 326.43, 6 past the end of the row of badges under Union Station's name. MARC is the last badge of that row, so the line goes on from it. It crosses the Purple Line, the DC boundary and the Beltway, and is drawn after the Metro lines in `draw_order`, so it is above the Purple Line near Glenridge, as the other commuter lines are above the Metro lines they cross. At New Carrollton it passes 24 from the Purple terminal; the link from the station's MARC badge marks the station.

ticks.note: the stations of the line as small ticks across it: a stroke 10 long and 3 wide, in the line's colour. New Carrollton has no tick: the link from its MARC badge (`connections`) marks it. Seabrook, Bowie State and Odenton, which only MARC serves, are on the ring to BWI (`marc-bwi-ring`), 66.22 apart, the first half a spacing past the corner at 330 deg and BWI's stopper a spacing past Odenton, with their names in the `place` font straight and outward along the radius (`rotate` the tick's angle less 360), starting 9 from the line, as on the Camden ring. Their distances along the line are not the ground's.

lines.badges_note: Only the line's stopper: a badge on this map marks a stop - a transfer at a Metro station, or the end of a commuter line - so the line has no badge of its own between Union Station and New Carrollton (an Amtrak and MARC row stood there, near the Anacostia); its colour and the legend name it. The ring to BWI has none of its own: the stopper at BWI is MARC's, with Amtrak's beside it (the airport's `connections`). The stopper at BWI: on the line's end, at theta 314.0 on `marc-bwi-ring`, level (`rotate` 0), its top 6 below the apron, which is moved so that it is centred over the badge.

lines.name: VRE from Union Station to L'Enfant Plaza
lines.note: a trial: the part of VRE that both its lines use, from Union Station to L'Enfant Plaza, in the blue of the VRE badge (#003D73), as the Manassas Line is. From Union Station's VRE badge, an L: in along the badge's radius (`vre-union`) to `vre-union-ring`, clockwise on that one ring outside Judiciary Sq's name, past the Capitol and under the east end of the National Mall, across the east trunk, down into the east trunk, ending at y 1052 under the Blue line's casing (theta 7.69), where `vre-long-bridge` goes on from the casing's bottom edge, level to L'Enfant Plaza's VRE badge and above the Yellow and Green lines. `under_geography`: it is drawn before the geography, so the Mall, which is widened to cover it, and the Capitol's icons are drawn over it, as the railway runs in a tunnel under Capitol Hill.

lines.name: VRE from below the east trunk to L'Enfant Plaza, across the Potomac and to King St-Old Town
lines.note: a trial: the VRE line from where `vre-core` comes out of the east trunk, at the Blue line's casing's bottom edge (y 1056, theta 8.29 on `vre-union-ring`), round the turn and west level at y 1059.5 (`vre-lenfant`'s `top` slot), in the upper half of L'Enfant Plaza's VRE badge, to the badge, under the station's two circles; from the badge's east end clockwise on a ring (`vre-potomac`), close inside the Yellow line's, across the Potomac, as the Long Bridge does, to the river's west bank; then straight down east of the Yellow line (`vre-alexandria`), through Crystal City's VRE badge to King St-Old Town's, both ON the line, where the Manassas Line goes on. A line of its own so that, unlike `vre-core`, it is drawn above the river, and last in `draw_order`, above the Yellow and Green lines it crosses on the way to L'Enfant Plaza.
lines.badges_note: L'Enfant Plaza's VRE badge, ON the line, where its level part turns onto the ring across the river: ON the level line (`vre-lenfant`, s 260.19), level, under the station's two circles (x 1260.19; the capsule runs from 1240 to 1293.23), at y 1062, its top (1055.5) 0.5 over the bottom of the Blue Line's white casing (1056) and 1.5 below the Blue Line's colour, with the turn onto the ring across the river under its east end, so the line comes in to its east end, its top edge 2 below the badge's top edge (`vre-lenfant`'s `top` slot, y 1059.5), and leaves it south from there, at x 1270.22, 3 inside the badge's east end (x 1273.19), which is about 1.4 clear of the Yellow line's casing (from about x 1274.6). It replaces the badge that stood under the station's name. The second is Crystal City's, ON the vertical straight east of the Yellow line (`vre-alexandria`, x 1011), level with its station (y 1415.31), turned to the ring through it (`rotate` -1.52): 26 long, about x 998 - 1024, so it overlaps the Yellow line's casing (1005) by about 7. islands.name: Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool

islands.name: East Potomac Park

islands.name: Old Town Alexandria

islands.note: Old Town Alexandria's waterfront as a pale yellow area, the fill of The Wharf, built as The Wharf's strip is: the waterfront anchor at its top and the name below it, reading top to bottom. It is against the Yellow line and starts across from Braddock Rd: its top, y = 1586.5, is level with the top of that station's dot. Its left edge is x = 1017, 12.25 east of the west edge of the bank trail (1004.75, at the Yellow line's casing, 1005), to make room for the VRE line between it and the Yellow line (x 1011). The Virginia bank has no free land here, so the area lies over the trail's full width, the bank (x = 1022.5) and 16 of the water, as the DCA apron does. islands.name: Potomac water taxi: Georgetown - The Wharf - Old Town - National Harbor
islands.note: the water taxi on the Potomac, as a thin white dashed line on the water - white as the Great Falls icon is - between the four waterfronts that have the anchor icon. Every turn is an arc that is tangent to the parts it joins. This part starts 5 from the boat off Georgetown Waterfront Park, goes straight out for 10.1, square to the bank and on the boat's own axis, and turns a quarter on an arc of radius 8 into the middle of the north-west arm and goes down it. Theodore Roosevelt Island is in the middle of the arm, and the river's main channel is on its District side, so the line goes round the island's north and east sides: it leaves the middle on an arc of radius 20 and follows a circle about the island's own centre, 6.3 off the island - in the middle of the water between the island and the District's bank - for 171 deg, down to the island's south-east. There an arc of radius 20 turns it into the middle of the water round the bulge, which is not a ring: the water's outer edge is the ring r 180, but its inner edge is the Tidal Basin shore (`park-tidal-basin`, a hand-drawn curve, its outer edge 17.35 from its line), 116 from the map's centre at the top of the bend and 132 at the bottom. So the line follows the middle of the two, (inner + 180) / 2, from r 148.03 at theta 169.97 to 155.96 at the bottom (theta 90), as eight cubic curves through the middle points every 10 deg, tangent at both ends; it was the ring r 148, which is the middle only at the top and was 8 too far in at the bottom. It turns into the south arm on a quarter of an ellipse, goes down the middle of the channel west of East Potomac Park (x = 1037.75), and below Hains Point one S curve takes it to the middle of the south arm, at (1083, 1470), where `ferry-wharf` and `ferry-national-harbor` meet it. Those two and `ferry-old-town` are each written FROM their boat, so that a whole dash starts 5 from each boat. They are in `geo.islands`, which is drawn above the water; the Metro lines cross over them. The service is seasonal, and its routes are the operator's, not surveyed here.

islands.name: Potomac water taxi, the part to National Harbor

islands.name: Potomac water taxi, the branch to The Wharf
islands.note: from the boat off The Wharf, in the middle of the Washington Channel (x = 1127.4), down the channel and on an S curve to the main line below Hains Point, at (1083, 1470). The curve is the mirror image of the main line's, so the two make a fork round Hains Point.

islands.name: Potomac water taxi, the branch to Old Town Alexandria
islands.note: a short level branch from the main line to the boat off the amber Old Town area (which ends at x = 1038.75), level with the area's anchor.

islands.name: West Potomac Park · Tidal Basin shore
islands.note: a hand-drawn green band that lies ON the Potomac arm, so it is emitted with the islands and not with the parks. It starts inside the National Mall at y = 960, above the north bank edge (y = 963.2 at the band's west side), so no water shows between the band and the Mall. It goes down and curves east to the top of East Potomac Park. The butt end stops 8 short, at x = 1030.45, and arrives horizontal; `park-tidal-basin-end` supplies the last 8 with rounded corners.

islands.name: West Potomac Park · rounded east end

The union is the 34.7 band ending at x = 1038.45 with two corners of radius 8, the radius the other parks use.

beltway.name: Capital Beltway

text.note: `size_px` is in the shield's own frame: with the shield's `scale` (1.119) the type is 12 px on the map.

shields.note: the Interstate 495 shield, in its official red and blue, as the first sign of each of the ring's two names: on the name's own line (`offset` from the ring, as the name has), turned with it (`rotate`) and 6 before its first letter. The names' widths are from Inter's own metrics (246 and 265), and each name is moved along the ring so that the shield and the name together are centred where the name alone was. The shape is traced from the road sign for a number of three figures, 25 wide and 19.66 high in its own frame with the origin at its centre: two shallow dips that meet in a point at the top, pointed top corners, a red crown that gets wider down to a white rule, and a blue field whose sides are one round curve from the rule to a blunt point at the bottom, with no straight part. `scale` 1.119 makes it 22 high and 28.0 wide, the size of a landmark icon: its top is 19 from the ring's centre line, on the names' side, and its point at the bottom goes across the ring to the ring's far edge, so the shield stands ON the road. Its `offset` (8) is thus less than the names'. Two more shields stand alone in the other two quadrants, with no name, and their centres are ON the ring's centre line (`offset` 0), so the ring goes through their middle: at 221.33 deg in the north-west, turned as a name outside the ring is, midway on the ring between the Potomac's north bank (213.89) and the MARC Brunswick Line beside the Red Line (228.77), 93.2 from each, and at 57 deg in the south-east, turned as a name inside the ring is, between Congress Heights' name and the District's boundary names; nothing is within 45 of the south-east one. The crown has no word in it. The number is in the map's bold type, made narrower (`squeeze`) to the width that the road sign's narrow figures have.

beltway.labels_note: type OUTSIDE the ring, centred at `angle`: one line that names the ring and the state it is in, `CAPITAL BELTWAY – MARYLAND` in the north-east and `CAPITAL BELTWAY – VIRGINIA` in the south-west. The states' names stood inside the ring, as lines of their own, before. `offset` puts the caps' centre 11.1 from the ring's centre line: 3 of ring half-width, 3 of paper, and 5.1 of half cap height. The ~260-wide bold text spans about 20 deg, and `half_span` is the carrier arc's length each side. The two copies sit in opposite quadrants.

labels.note: the name and the 495 shield before it are ONE block, 6 apart, and the block's middle is at 139.5: the name's own middle is thus 138.14, 16.99 along the ring from it. 139.5 is the middle of the free stretch 116 - 162 deg on the 1.5 grid; the name spans about 129 - 150. `offset` -13.1 puts it INSIDE the ring, where the paper is free: outside, the VRE line to Manassas runs on a ring 28 from the Beltway and the name was between the two. In the map's lower half the type runs counter-clockwise with its top toward the ring, so it reads left to right and upward.

the name and the 495 shield before it are ONE block, 6 apart, and the block's middle is at 310.5: the name's own middle is thus 311.84, 16.99 along the ring from it. 310.5 is the middle, on the 1.5 grid, of the free stretch between the two terminal groups at this radius: Greenbelt's Green terminal ends at 291.0 deg and New Carrollton's Purple terminal starts at 330.9. boundary_labels.note: the names of the three jurisdictions, in the grey of the Beltway's name. The District's and Maryland's stand on the two sides of the boundary, each `offset` 8.5 off the line, as two groups whose names share one edge on one radius (`align`): the south group's names START at theta 76.0, their left edge, and the north-west group's START at theta 219.0, also their left edge. The south group is on the boundary's south ring (r = 664), its District name centred near theta 69.0, in the one long stretch of the boundary that no station label crosses, between the end of Congress Heights' label (theta 62) and the Potomac (theta 77). The north-west group is on the main ring (r = 590) in its first stretch, between the Potomac and the Red line, above Georgetown Waterfront Park: the boundary leaves the river at theta 211.5 and the Red line's casing is at 229.8. The names start at 219.0, on the 1.5 grid and about 12 past the park's inland edge (217.8 at this radius), and the longest, `DISTRICT OF`, ends near 228.4, about 14 short of the Red line's casing; Friendship Heights' and Tenleytown-AU's own names are east of the line. The group was at theta 255.8, in the white between those two names and the west edge of Rock Creek Park. At the font's 12 the District's name in one line (160) is as long as the whole stretch, so it is two concentric lines, `DISTRICT OF` and `COLUMBIA`, 10.5 apart - 1.8 of white between the two lines of capitals. In the north-east every stretch of the ring is crossed by a slanted station label. The Maryland - West Virginia boundary (`md-wv-boundary`, r 1045.2), where the Brunswick Line crosses it between Brunswick and Harpers Ferry, has short names, `MD` inside and `WV` outside, 8.5 off the line, on the radial's lower side: they END at theta 217.98, their right edge, about 35 past the end of Harpers Ferry's name (219.86), whose ring WV shares, and past Brunswick's (220.8), whose ring MD shares, about 2.1 deg from the boundary's lower end (214.88). Virginia has no boundary line - the Potomac is the boundary - so its name is there twice. One is straight type on the river's Virginia bank, parallel to the water (37.5) and 14 outside the bank's green; it, the river's name and Georgetown Waterfront's name are centred on one line across the river. The other is in the Beltway's own name outside the ring in the south-west, `CAPITAL BELTWAY – VIRGINIA`, and Maryland's is in the north-east one (`geo.beltway.labels`).

landmarks.note: tiny pictograms of the map's landmarks, each a filled silhouette authored in its own frame - about 24 across, origin at its centre - and moved to `at` by a translate; an optional `scale` sizes one icon about that centre. They are one flat grey (contrast about 6:1 on park green, 8:1 on paper) and filled even-odd, so a sub-path inside the outline is a hole: columns, windows, the Pentagon's court. Pure geography - each `at` keeps at least 17 clear of every line casing, marker and station label.

items.name: US Capitol
items.note: the Capitol's dome on a plinth, this map's own drawing: the statue as a small figure on a foot; the lantern - a cap, a cornice and a drum with three slots on a flared base; the dome, taller than a half circle and flared at its foot, with a row of nine windows; and two rings of columns as floating tiers, seven arched openings in the upper ring and nine in the lower, each 0.94 wide in this frame so that they stay open at map size. The frame is 20 across and 24.4 high. Inside the National Mall's east end, which stops at Capitol South's x = 1386: at `scale` 1.5 it is 30 across and 36.6 high. It is centred in the patch of the Mall east of the Green line: the line's casing is at x = 1324.2 at this y and the Mall ends at 1386, so the icon keeps 15.9 on each side. The Library of Congress is on the other side of the edge.

items.name: White House
items.note: the north front as WMATA's map draws it: a roof line that bows up over the portico, a second line under it, and the wall below, with four gaps for the portico's columns and a block of four windows in each wing. 24 across and 11.4 high about its own centre. In the part of the White House park that stands above the National Mall (y 857.3 - 912), in its upper part: the icon's ink is 16 below the park's top edge and 27.5 above the Mall's, centred where the ink of the earlier pediment icon was.

items.name: Lincoln Memorial
items.note: a flat-roofed temple: six columns between a stepped base and an entablature with an attic, no pediment. At `scale` 1.1 it is 26.4 across and 19.25 high: at its own size, 24 across, it was small beside the Washington Monument and the Capitol. At the National Mall's west end, with its east edge at x = 921, 12 before the reflecting pool, and on the Mall's centre line (y = 950), above the Tidal Basin's park band.

items.name: Washington Monument
items.note: an obelisk on a low base. On the White House's axis in the National Mall. At `scale` 1.5 it is 36 tall, the tallest icon on the Mall as the obelisk is on the ground - a little taller than the Capitol's 34.5; its centre is on the Mall's centre line (y = 950), so it has 19 of green above it and its base (968) keeps 5.5 above the Tidal Basin's dome (y = 973.5).

items.name: Pentagon
items.note: a regular pentagon of radius 11 with its court of radius 5, and one thin pentagon slot (radius 7.5 to 8.5) through the middle of the wall: two of the building's five rings, with a line of light between them. At `scale` 1.25 it is 26 across and the slot is 1 wide. On paper north-west of the Pentagon station, in the middle of the white between the Blue line and Arlington Cemetery: at r = 259.5, half-way between the Blue ring's casing (230) and the caps of the station's name (288.9), and at theta 108, half-way between the casing of the Blue line on the south corridor (99 at this radius) and the cemetery's edge (117). `rotate` 18 turns it to the tangent of its own circle there (108 - 90), which is the direction of the station's concentric name below it, so the icon's flat base is parallel to the type.

items.name: Washington National Cathedral
items.note: the Gothic west front: two towers with paired pinnacles, a gabled nave between them, a rose window and a pointed door. West of Cleveland Park, on the side of the Red line its labels leave free.

items.name: Basilica of the National Shrine
items.note: the great dome with its cross, beside the tall campanile. West of the Red line beside Rhode Island Av, inside the turn the line makes toward Fort Totten. It stood at [1296, 572]; Fort Totten's label is now below the Red arc and ends beside that place, so the icon moved 19 west and 14 south, to r = 498. It is now beside Brookland-CUA, as the basilica is on the ground: at r = 537.5, theta 305.88, in the corner that the Red arc and the Red spoke make, 36.2 from the station. It is nearer to the lines than the 17 that the other icons' centres keep, by eye: the point of the drawing's top is 0.3 from the casing of the arc, 2.3 from its red, and its side is 3.2 from the casing of the spoke, 5.2 from its red.

items.name: Library of Congress
items.note: an open book, not the building: the Jefferson Building is a dome on a block and would read as a second Capitol. The slot is the gutter between the two pages. On paper just east of the National Mall, on the museums' south row (y = 966), below the Supreme Court's gavel and on its centre line (x = 1405). At `scale` 0.8 the book is 17.6 across: the Mall stops at Capitol South's x = 1386 and the book starts 8.2 past that edge, so the Mall's end separates the two icons. Its centre is 17 west of Eastern Market (x = 1420).

items.name: Jefferson Memorial
items.note: a rotunda in the memorial's own proportions, taken from a photograph: of the 22 width, the colonnade is 7.4 high (eight tall columns, seven gaps), the entablature above it 2.2 and the widest part, two attic steps come in to 0.78 and 0.69 of the width, and the dome is a low cap, 0.6 of the width across and only 4.2 high - a saucer and not a half circle. The low dome on the wide ring is what tells it from the Lincoln Memorial and from the Capitol. At the north end of East Potomac Park, on the island's centre line, with the same 16.75 of green above the dome as at each side of the base - the tip of the peninsula that faces the Tidal Basin.

items.name: Smithsonian National Zoo
items.note: a paw print: one pad and four toes. In Rock Creek Park, where the zoo is, in the lower part of the rect - the end nearest Woodley Park - and 66 below the park's name.

items.name: US National Arboretum
items.note: a broadleaf tree: a crown of seven lobes, 19 across, on a short trunk that flares at its foot - a plain disc on a stick read as a lollipop. At `scale` 0.65 it is about 12 across. In the arboretum wedge, centred over the park's name on x = 1469.5; icon and name are one stack a little above the wedge's middle.

items.name: Kenilworth Park & Aquatic Gardens
items.note: a lotus flower of five petals, for the aquatic gardens, in the landmarks' own grey. It stands on the DC boundary, in the visible green of the Kenilworth wedge: at r = 590, the boundary's own ring, so the line of dots runs into the icon's middle from each side, and at theta = 343.75, the middle of the wedge's angle span (340 - 347.5). `scale` 0.7 makes it about 17 across and 11 high; the river's casing (560) is 24 below it and the Orange line's casing (609) 13 above it. The icon has a `halo`: an outline in the park's green under the shape, 8.6 wide in the icon's own frame and so 3 at this scale all round it, which takes the dots away where they would touch it.

items.name: The Wharf
items.note: an anchor: ring, shank, stock, and two curved arms that end in flukes. The other waterfronts reuse this shape (`like`). In the amber `area-the-wharf` on the DC bank of the Washington Channel, above the area's name; at `scale` 0.8 the anchor is 18.2 across, and it keeps the same 7.9 of amber above it as at each side.

items.name: Georgetown waterfront
items.note: the waterfront anchor, upright, at the east end of Georgetown Waterfront Park, where the boats are on the ground - the harbour is at the mouth of Rock Creek: on the park's centre line, 6 west of the Rock Creek band.

items.name: The Yards
items.note: the waterfront anchor in the amber `area-the-yards`, on its mid ring (r = 491) at theta 43.56 - the end nearest Navy Yard-Ballpark - before the area's name. The anchor is 18.2 across in the 34-deep strip and keeps 7.9 of amber on each side, as The Wharf's does.

items.name: Old Town Alexandria waterfront
items.note: the waterfront anchor for Old Town Alexandria, at the top of the amber `area-old-town` and above its name, placed as The Wharf's is in its area: on the strip's centre line, 17.2 below the strip's top, with the same 7.9 of amber above it as at each side. It is across from Braddock Rd, where the strip starts.

items.name: National Harbor
items.note: the waterfront anchor in the amber `area-national-harbor`, placed as The Wharf's is in its area: on the strip's centre line (x = 1164.5, The Wharf's own x), 17.2 below the strip's top, above the area's name, with the same 7.9 of amber above it as at each side.

items.name: Great Falls of the Potomac
items.note: three white waves, one above the other, for the rapids of the falls - foam on the water. Each is a wavy band 16 across and 2.8 deep with 2.8 of water between two of them; one wave is 8 long and 1.2 high, and the three are in phase. Each band starts 4 to the right of the one above it, so the sign is a diagonal that goes down to the right, as the river runs on this map. The frame is 24 across and 16.4 high. It is in the water, in the middle of the Potomac's NW arm, 262.5 down the arm from its mouth, immediately outside the Capital Beltway (300), as the falls are: its end is about 20 from the ring's edge. The arm is about 71 wide there, so the icon has about 23 of water at each side. It is after the name `Great Falls` (`geo-label-great-falls`), about 12 clear of it. It has no `scale`: white on the water's blue is a weak contrast (about 1.9:1), so the icon is at its full size.

items.name: Potomac water taxi, Georgetown
items.note: the Potomac water taxi from the side, bow to the left, traced from a photograph of the boat and kept to three shapes. One outline is the hull and the cabin: a stem that is almost upright, a bow that flares up to the top of the side, a wheelhouse front that is raked back to its roof, the long cabin behind it, the open deck aft of the cabin at the height of the side, and a stern that slopes down to a low platform at the water. A slot in the cabin is its long strip of dark windows (the outline fills it). A thin slab above is the roof, which starts behind the wheelhouse, one step higher, and goes on past the cabin over the open deck. The lengths are the boat's own; the heights are 2.2 times its own, because the boat is seven times as long as it is high and would be a line at this size. In yellow, the colour of the boats, with a dark blue outline (its `halo`, 1.1 wide at this scale) that sets the yellow off the water. The frame is 24 long and 7.5 high; at `scale` 0.75 the boat is 18 long and 5.6 high. One stands on the water at the landing of the dashed water taxi line off each of the four waterfronts that have the anchor icon; this one is off Georgetown Waterfront Park, 10 from the bank. The others reuse the shape (`like`).

items.name: Potomac water taxi, The Wharf
items.note: the water taxi boat in the middle of the Washington Channel, off The Wharf, level with The Wharf's anchor (y = 1303.2), at the end of the branch `ferry-wharf`.

items.name: Potomac water taxi, Old Town Alexandria
items.note: the water taxi boat off the amber Old Town area, 3 from its edge (x = 1051) and level with the area's anchor (y = 1603.7), at the end of the branch `ferry-old-town`.

items.name: Potomac water taxi, National Harbor
items.note: the water taxi boat off National Harbor, 4 from the bank (x = 1144.3) and level with National Harbor's anchor (y = 1735.2), at the end of the main line `ferry-potomac`.

items.name: RFK Stadium
items.note: a football, for the team whose home the stadium was: a pointed oval 23 long and 12.8 across, tilted 35 deg, with a white stripe near each point and the laces along its middle - a seam crossed by four ties. At `scale` 1.2 it is about 28 long. On the Capitol's own y (954) - the stadium closes the east end of East Capitol Street, the Mall's axis carried on past the Capitol - on the Anacostia's west bank at r = 486, under the arboretum, which was moved up the river to clear it. It keeps 20 above the east trunk's Orange casing and 36 clear of Stadium-Armory's marker.

items.name: Nationals Park
items.note: a baseball: a disc with its two seams as curved slots. items.name: Capital One Arena
items.note: two crossed hockey sticks with a puck between their blades, for the Capitals. The sticks cross at a right angle - each is at 45 deg - with shafts 3 thick. Each stick is an L: its foot turns level through a rounded heel into a blade 3.6 deep and 8.4 long with a round tip, not a square block. The longer blades make the icon 29 across, so it is drawn at `scale` 0.85 to keep its old footprint. The sticks overlap where they cross, so this one icon is filled `nonzero` - both sticks are wound the same way and the crossing stays solid, where the even-odd rule of the other icons would cut a hole in it. The arena is at Gallery Place, but that interchange is ringed by lines and labels: the nearest free paper is 44 north of it, in the angle between the Green/Yellow and the Red line: at r = 341.2, theta 304.51, where the ink of the drawing is 2 from the Green ring's casing (328) and 2 from the Red spoke's - nearer than the 17 that the other icons' centres keep, by eye. It was 59 from the station before the Green ring moved in to 316.

items.name: National Museum of American History
items.note: a flag on its pole, for the Star-Spangled Banner the museum holds: a solid canton and four slots that leave five stripes. Its own `scale` is 0.65: a rectangle on a full-height pole fills the corners of its box, so at the row's 0.75 it looked larger than its round and pointed neighbours. The eight museums stand in two rows on the National Mall, at `scale` 0.75 but for this one (0.65), the African American museum (1) and the Hirshhorn (0.95): those two are low, wide buildings, and at the row's scale they were only 9.6 and 12.3 high beside icons of 14 to 18. The rows are at y = 928.5 and y = 971.5, 21.5 above and below the Mall's centre line (y = 950; the Mall is y 912 - 988 since its top edge was moved 8 north). The icons' drawings are not all centred on their own origins and are not one height, so each `at` is set from the drawing's own box: the BOTTOM of every icon is on one line, as buildings on one ground line: y = 936 in the north row, where the tallest icon, Natural History, has 8.6 of green above it, and y = 979.5 in the south row, 8.5 above the Mall's bottom edge; with the Mall's own name between them. The north row is the Mall's north side: four icons spread evenly from x = 1046 to 1177.2, 43.7 apart, in their order on the ground. The south row is its south side: four icons on the same four columns, also in their order on the ground. The single shapes on the Mall - Lincoln Memorial, reflecting pool and Capitol - sit on its centre line, y = 950; the Washington Monument's centre is 1 above it. This one is second in the north row.

items.name: Smithsonian Castle
items.note: the Castle's two entrance towers, after the building itself: on the left the shorter tower under a steep spire with concave sides and a finial, on the right the taller tower with a flat, slightly wider head and two tall arched windows, and a small gable between them over the joined base. items.name: National Air and Space Museum

items.name: National Gallery of Art

items.name: National Museum of African American History and Culture
items.note: the building's corona seen from a corner, so it reads as a solid block and not as a flat cup: a wide front face and a narrower side face meet at a vertical corner, marked by a slot at x = 4, and the roof line and the two tier joints fall away from that corner on both faces. Three tiers of equal height, each flaring outward as it rises, on a recessed glass base and a ground line. First in the north row, east of the corner the White House park's east edge (x = 1034.6) makes with the Mall's top edge.

items.name: National Museum of Natural History
items.note: a long-necked dinosaur in profile, for the fossil halls: a tail that tapers to the left and is held off the ground, a round body that stands on one leg below the hips and one below the shoulders, with the belly's curve between them, and a neck that rises to a small head at the upper right. Third in the north row, between American History and the National Gallery of Art.

items.name: National Museum of Asian Art
items.note: a seated Buddha, from the front, in meditation: the head with its top knot, the shoulders, the two arms held off the body by a thin slot each and meeting in the lap, and the crossed legs as a wide base with a curved slot above them. First in the south row, below the African American museum.

items.name: Hirshhorn Museum
items.note: the building as a cylinder seen from a little above, so it reads as round: an elliptical top with the open court as a hole in it, a curved slot along the front rim that parts the top from the wall, straight sides, the long balcony slot in the wall, and a curved foot on three short, thick piers. Third in the south row, between the Castle and Air and Space as on the ground.

service_patterns.note: the parts of a line that only some of its trains serve, as WMATA's own map marks them `Served by every other train`: the Yellow line north of Mt Vernon Sq, where every other train turns back, and the two east branches of the Silver line, which its trains take by turns. Each section is drawn right after its line - over the line's colour and under every line drawn later - as a second stroke of the line's own width in `stroke`, dashed by `dasharray`: white bars across the line, 2.5 wide, with 9 of the line's colour between them. A section's `segments` are in the lines' own vocabulary and repeat that part of the line's route, from the last station that every train serves.

connections.note: other railways a Metro station connects to, each as a small badge in the service's colour with its name in white capitals. A badge is PART OF ITS STATION'S LABEL, as the P and the hospital cross are, and has no co-ordinates: an item names its `station` and its `services`, and the generator puts the badges at that label, so they move with it. There are three places. `left` and `right` set the badge in the label's own line, before or after the name - beyond the marks when it is on their side. `bottom` draws the badges as a row of rounded rects under the last line of type, `badge.below_dy` from its baseline to their middle, on the edge the label is anchored to and turned with the label; `top` draws the same row over the first line, `badge.above_dy` from its baseline to their middle: the 14 px name's ascenders (about 10.5), 3 of white, as under a name, and half the badge. The default is `bottom`; an item's `place` selects another. The colours are dark and muted on purpose, so no badge reads as a Metro line.

inline.note: a badge in a label's line is drawn as a station mark is: `box` is Inter's filled square at the marks' size and stroke, 13.7 across, set as many times as the service's `width` needs and stepped so that the strokes join into one bar of exactly that width; the service's name is drawn back over the middle of the bar, which needs its own length (`services[].text_width`, from Inter Bold's advances at the badge font's 8 px). `box_advance_em` and `box_ink_em` are the square's metrics in Inter Bold, the ones the parking mark's note quotes. `rise` lifts the 8 px name to the middle of the bar: half the bar's cap height (5.1) less half the name's (2.9).

legend.note: the map's key, in the corners the circular diagram leaves free on the square canvas: the map's sign and title with WMATA's contact lines at the top left, the seven lines, the service pattern and the accessibility line at the bottom left, the symbols and the credits at the bottom right and the north sign at the top right. Reference material sits below the map, where a reader goes to it second. Every sample in the symbol key is drawn from the same constants as the thing it stands for, so the key cannot drift from the map. A row's centre is `row_height` below the one above; type is set with its capitals centred on the row. A key's `heading_dy` lifts its heading off the row grid: -8 leaves about twice a row's white under the heading, so it reads as the block's title and not as its first row.

logo.note: this map's own sign: a bold square M that is made of concentric rings over a tunnel - the map's idea and the station's vault in one figure. `d` is the clip outline in a 100-unit box, which it fills from edge to edge, in two sub-paths that wind the same way and so add up: the letter (stems 25 wide, a flat foot of the same width under the V, the V's notch down to 50.7) and a half disc of radius 25 on the middle of the base line, which makes the bottom ring a round tunnel mouth and not a keystone. The outline is not drawn; it clips three rings about `centre`, the middle of the base line, each given as its inner and outer radius: the tunnel, the ring over it, and a third that runs past the letter's top corners, so the upper half is two solid blocks with the V between them. The two white arcs are 8.7 wide, and each lies on a sharp point of the letter - the inner foot of the stems (r = 25) and the tips of the two white triangles under the diagonals (r = 72.36). The upper arc is that high so that the three dark parts are near one height on the sign's centre line - tunnel 25, middle ring 30, top blocks 28 - where a lower arc made it top-heavy. The sign is `size` wide and high and is drawn in the legend's ink. `size` 104.8 and `dy` 40 put its top on the top of the title's capitals (y = 65.6) and its bottom on the base line of the last header line (y = 170.4); the text starts `gap` to its right.

title.align_note: `text_dx`, `notes_dx` and `contact.dx` take out each line's own side bearing - the white a font leaves before a first letter, which grows with the type's size and differs by letter (D, I, M, S) - so the INK of all four header lines starts on one edge, x = 186.8, the header's `gap` from the logo.

contact.note: WMATA's contact lines, directly under the title and on the title's own left edge: the two lines of numbers. The title is as large as the space over the numbers lets it be. The title's `notes` line - what the map is - comes last, below them (`title.first_dy` 88). The block ends at about y = 177, 19 above the Shady Grove label, whose box starts at x = 425.

symbols.heading: Symbols
symbols.note: the line key's mirror image, set against the canvas's right margin: one narrow column of samples on the right, 46 wide and ending 60 from the canvas edge, each sample flush to the column's RIGHT edge (`symbol_align` end) - the margin that the heading, the rule and the credits also end on, as the line key's dots stand on the left margin; and one column of type to its left that ENDS on a common right edge (`text_anchor` end, `text_dx` -12). The white between a name and its sample is 12 at the widest sample, the AMTRAK badge at 43, and more at the narrower ones. The heading ends on the margin (`heading_dx`). No sample is wider than the column, which is why each railway has a row of its own and the landmarks are one example icon. Its own `row_height` 30 replaces the legend's 36: the samples and the type are smaller than the line key's, and 30 still keeps 4 between the two tallest samples, the station and the transfer station, which are in adjacent rows.

accessible.note: the accessibility statement, directly below the line key at the bottom left: the wheelchair sign centred on `at`, with its left edge on the canvas's 60 margin, then a line of section type that starts `text_dx` to its right. The sign is the International Symbol of Access in the open form that transit maps use: a seated figure and the wheel as an open arc. It is a filled outline in a 24-unit box (21.5 across, 24 high), scaled by `scale`. The sign runs from y = 1906 to y = 1940, the canvas's bottom margin, 30 below the sample of the last row of the line key.

credits.note: the copyright line and the disclaimer, below the symbol key at the bottom right, ending on the canvas's 60 margin (`anchor` end): two lines of legend text type in the grey of the Beltway's name, `line_dy` apart, the first centred on `at`, under a thin `rule` of the symbol key's width that sets them off from the key. The disclaimer is there because the map carries WMATA's logo, name and contact lines. The map's version is at the end of the second line, which is the shorter one, so the block stays inside the rule's width; it is written here by hand for each edition.

north.note: the north sign, in the top corner opposite the Metro sign: an ink arrow 52 tall and 35 across over an ink N, with no ring or disc. `at` is the arrow's centre. Its top is at y = 60 and its right point at x = 1940, so it keeps the same 60 from the top and the right edge of the canvas as every other block of the key keeps from its edges; with the N it runs down to y = 135.

layers.note: `draw_order` lists `lines[].id` values; each one is drawn twice, white casing (30) first, then the coloured stroke (26) - 18 and 14 for the Purple line. A later line therefore crosses an earlier one with a 2 px white gap.

checks.note: Only the bounds an assertion needs as a parameter are stored here; the rest of what a spec reader can assert without any SVG is carried by the generator alone. See SPEC.md §9.

curve_geometry.note: asserted on every curved line of type: an arc stays a minor arc, and no line sits closer to the centre than min_line_radius_px (14 px of cap height would shear). min_line_radius_px binds radial labels too, on the base point each reads outward from; max_span_deg does not, a radius having no span.
